claims.text: Solidified equiatomic FeNiCrMn is single-phase after homogenization.
The prepared polycrystalline FeNiCrMn has a uniform initial microstructure.
The dynamic mechanical behavior of equiatomic FeNiCrMn is primarily controlled by temperature- and strain-rate-dependent activation of deformation twinning.
Lower temperatures limit dislocation mobility in FeNiCrMn.
Higher strain rates suppress conventional dislocation glide in FeNiCrMn.
Suppression of dislocation glide at low temperature and high strain rate activates deformation twinning.
Deformation twins act as barriers to dislocation slip.
Deformation twins partition strain in FeNiCrMn.
Deformation twinning increases work hardening in FeNiCrMn.
Deformation twinning increases ductility in FeNiCrMn.
At higher temperatures or lower strain rates, dislocation slip dominates deformation in FeNiCrMn.
Slip-dominated deformation at higher temperatures or lower strain rates produces lower work-hardening rates.
Low-temperature, high-strain-rate tests will produce higher yield strength than room-temperature quasi-static tests.
Low-temperature, high-strain-rate tests will produce greater strain hardening than room-temperature quasi-static tests.
Low-temperature, high-strain-rate tests will produce a higher deformation-twin density than room-temperature quasi-static tests.
Room-temperature, quasi-static loading produces moderate strength and strain hardening with minimal observable deformation twinning.
Secondary phases, pre-existing defects, or processing-induced microstructural variation may change the dominant deformation mechanism.
Dynamic strain aging or phase transformations may also contribute to the dynamic response of FeNiCrMn.
Direct mechanistic evidence specific to FeNiCrMn is limited.

contradictions.description: The material is alternately described as homogenized and as-solidified. Homogenization is a post-solidification heat treatment, so a homogenized specimen is not strictly in the as-solidified condition.
